subject: radiology
title: Emergency nephrostomy and antegrade stents

steps.tx: An infected blocked kidney deteriorates quickly and needs pus drained within hours. **Obstructive pyelonephritis** with fever, pain and an obstructing stone is the classic presentation. **Percutaneous nephrostomy** under ultrasound drains the infected system and saves the kidney and the patient. Pregnancy with obstructing stones favours nephrostomy over radiation heavy surgery. Fluids and antibiotics run alongside drainage as part of **sepsis care** and never replace drainage.
steps.say: An infected blocked kidney deteriorates quickly and needs pus drained within hours. Fever with pain and an obstructing stone is the classic presentation here. Nephrostomy under ultrasound drains the infected system and saves kidney function. Fluids and antibiotics run alongside drainage and never replace urgent drainage in sepsis.

steps.tx: The kidney ultrasound shows a markedly **dilated pelvicalyceal system** with black urine filled spaces that indicate hydronephrosis. A bright upper ureteric stone casts a dark **posterior acoustic shadow** and marks the level of obstruction. Infected urine cannot escape past the stone, so **obstructive pyelonephritis** develops under pressure. This appearance is the classic indication for urgent nephrostomy in examination questions.
steps.say: The kidney ultrasound shows a dilated collecting system that indicates hydronephrosis clearly. A bright ureteric stone is visible because it casts a shadow at the obstruction. Infected urine cannot escape past the stone and builds pressure inside. This appearance is the classic indication for urgent nephrostomy drainage in examinations.

vis.alt: Kidney ultrasound showing dilated pelvicalyceal system, upper ureteric stone shadowing and nephrostomy indication.
vis.caption: Renal ultrasound shows dilated system with obstructing ureteric stone. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Internal drainage follows once infection has settled and the kidney recovers. **Antegrade ureteric stenting** pushes a double J stent down past the stone or stricture into the bladder. A **nephrostogram** maps the ureter before any stenting attempt is made. A tight stricture that cannot be crossed keeps the nephrostomy until definitive surgery is planned. Patients are warned that a stent commonly causes **urinary frequency** and loin ache after placement.
steps.say: Internal drainage follows once infection has settled and the kidney recovers. Antegrade stenting pushes a double J stent past the block into the bladder. A dye study maps the ureter before any attempt is made. A tight stricture keeps the nephrostomy in place, and patients need warning about frequency and loin ache.

steps.tx: A blocked nephrostomy tube declares itself loudly and needs prompt action. **Falling output** with pain and fever suggests a clotted or displaced tube that needs exchange. Flushing that meets resistance must stop because force can burst the collecting system. Urine leaking around the tube causes **skin excoriation** and needs repositioning with skin care. A tube pulled out through a mature tract reseats easily, while a fresh tract needs repuncture.
steps.say: A blocked nephrostomy tube declares itself loudly and needs prompt action. Falling output with pain and fever suggests clotting or displacement clearly. Flushing that meets resistance must stop because force damages the kidney. Leaking urine damages skin and needs repositioning, while a mature tract reseats more easily than a fresh tract.

vis.alt: A diagram showing common nephrostomy tube problems: blockage, displacement causing urinary leak and skin irritation, and accidental pull-out.
vis.caption: Common nephrostomy tube complications and troubleshooting

steps.tx: Definitive stone treatment waits until the kidney is calm and urine is sterile. **Definitive stone surgery** follows some weeks after sepsis resolves and infection clears. Short term stents may be removed with strings, while **forgotten stents** encrust and block. An encrusted stent needs staged endoscopic treatment and must never be pulled blindly. Generous fluids and a **metabolic workup** reduce the chance of further stone formation.
steps.say: Definitive stone treatment waits until the kidney is calm and urine is sterile. Stone surgery follows some weeks after sepsis resolves completely. Short term stents may leave with strings, while forgotten stents encrust badly. An encrusted stent needs staged treatment, and fluids with metabolic testing reduce recurrence risk.
